action.boot.bcd: Rebuild the Windows boot configuration (BCD) for {windows}. Windows will rebuild it again by itself at its first start, to be sure.
action.boot.copy_files: Copy the Windows startup files back to the boot partition {esp}, from {windows}. Files of other systems (Linux...) are not touched.
action.boot.fallback: Add the backup startup file (EFI\Boot\bootx64.efi) so the PC finds Windows even if the BIOS forgets its entry.
action.boot.nvram: Recreate the "Windows Boot Manager" startup entry in the BIOS (disk {disk}, partition {partition}). Your files will not be touched.
action.boot.nvram_order: Re-enable the Windows startup entry Boot{num} and put it back in the BIOS startup list.
action.health.gpu_service_start: Re-enable the graphics driver "{driver}" (service {service}) so Windows loads it again.
action.health.post_script: Prepare an automatic repair that will run at the next Windows sign-in (system file check, graphics driver).
action.health.quarantine_dll: Move the damaged file {file} to C:\winbootfix_quarantine (it is not deleted and can be put back).
advice.backup_target: Plug in another USB drive (FAT32, exFAT or NTFS), or use a USB stick made with Rufus or Ventoy, then try again. Experts: --backup-dir.
advice.bitlocker: Find your 48-digit recovery key (on https://account.microsoft.com/devices/recoverykey, on paper or with your IT department), then choose Expert mode > BitLocker, or run: winbootfix --bitlocker-key ask. Without the key, nothing can be repaired from Linux.
advice.boot.ca2011_revoked: Update Windows from another way (WinPE, installation media) or temporarily disable Secure Boot in the BIOS.
advice.boot.copy_files: They can be copied back from Windows itself.
advice.boot.esp_missing: The partition may have been deleted. winbootfix never creates or formats partitions: use the WinPE variant or ask for help with the report.
advice.boot.nvram: The entry can be recreated without touching your files.
advice.boot.nvram_unreadable: Make sure the USB stick was started in UEFI mode.
advice.health.dll_quarantine: The file can be moved to quarantine; then reinstall: {software}.
advice.health.dll_system: This is a Windows file: it will be repaired by the system file check (DISM and SFC) at the next sign-in. Then reinstall if needed: {software}.
advice.health.gpu_download: The official driver will be proposed for download from Windows.
advice.health.gpu_post: The automatic repair at the next Windows sign-in will reinstall the driver.
advice.health.integrity: The system file check (DISM and SFC) will run at the next sign-in. If Windows does not start, use the WinPE variant for an offline repair.
advice.health.pending_xml: Let Windows finish it at the next start. If Windows stays stuck, the WinPE variant can cancel the pending update.
advice.system.dirty: Windows will check the disk at its next start. This is normal.
advice.system.hibernated: Startup can still be repaired. To repair inside Windows, start Windows if possible and choose Shut down while holding the Shift key, or allow the removal of the hibernation file (the open session is lost, your files are not).
advice.system.legacy_windows: Use the Windows installation media (Repair your computer > Command Prompt: bootrec /fixmbr, bootrec /fixboot, bootrec /rebuildbcd) or ask for help with the report.
advice.system.no_disk: Your disk controller is probably in VMD, Intel RST or RAID mode. See the BIOS advice above, and put the setting back as it was before starting Windows again.
advice.system.no_windows: Check that the right disk is connected. If Windows is on a disk not shown, the disk controller may be in RST/RAID mode.
advice.system.usb_legacy: Restart and choose the USB stick entry that starts with "UEFI:" in the boot menu (key F8, F11, F12 or Esc depending on the PC).
advice.winpe: Use the WinPE variant (Windows repair USB stick) described in the guide.

cli.command: what to do (see the list below)
cli.description:
winbootfix repairs two common Windows problems from Linux:
  1. the "Windows Boot Manager" entry disappeared from the BIOS and the PC no longer starts Windows;
  2. Windows starts but works badly (graphics driver not loaded, wrong or damaged DLL files, damaged system files).

By default it only diagnoses and changes nothing.
cli.epilog:
Commands:
  all           diagnose (and with --apply repair) startup and Windows health (default)
  boot          startup only
  health        Windows health only
  report        diagnostic only, write the report
  restore DIR   undo the changes saved in a backup folder
  list-backups  list backup folders
  menu          menu of the bootable USB stick

Examples:
  sudo winbootfix
  sudo winbootfix --apply
  sudo winbootfix boot --apply --expert --esp /dev/nvme0n1p1

Exit codes: 0 nothing to do, 1 problems found, 2 repaired, 3 partly repaired, 4 cancelled,
10 not root, 11 not UEFI, 12 no Windows, 13 BitLocker, 14 no disk, 15 ARM64, 16 no backup place,
64 bad usage, 70 internal error.
cli.expert: expert mode: technical details, one confirmation per action
cli.json: also print the report as JSON
cli.target: backup folder for the restore command
cli.windows_first: put Windows first in the BIOS startup order, even if another system was first

finding.health.gpu_service_missing: The graphics driver "{driver}" is referenced but its service ({service}) has disappeared.

finding.health.gpu_sys_missing: The graphics driver file is missing for "{driver}" ({file}).
finding.health.gpu_unknown: Windows has never installed a driver for the {vendor} graphics card ({hwid}).
finding.health.gpu_unreadable: The graphics driver settings could not be read.
finding.health.hive_dirty: The registry file {hive} was not closed cleanly (common after a crash).
finding.health.integrity_ok: No sign of damaged system files.
finding.health.pending_xml: A Windows update is still waiting to be finished (pending.xml).
finding.health.reboot_pending: Windows is waiting for a restart to finish an update.
finding.system.arm64: This Windows is for ARM processors (ARM64): not supported yet.
finding.system.bitlocker_other: Partition {partition} is encrypted with BitLocker and was not examined.
finding.system.bitlocker_suspended: Partition {partition} uses BitLocker in suspended or "waiting for activation" mode: it was opened without a key, read-only.
finding.system.dirty: The Windows disk was not closed properly last time.
finding.system.hibernated: Windows was not completely shut down (fast startup or hibernation).
finding.system.legacy_windows: This Windows is installed in old BIOS (Legacy/MBR) mode. Repairing this mode is not supported yet.
finding.system.usb_legacy: The USB stick was started in old BIOS (Legacy) mode, but Windows uses UEFI mode. The startup cannot be repaired in this mode.
finding.system.win_rw_blocked: Repairs inside Windows were skipped because Windows is in hibernation.
